- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 5–15% for next 7–14 days.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.3) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 3–8% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.  
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon; apply 2–5% upward bias for first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.  
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3–5 days, model lags; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment shift by +3–7% in next 3–7 days.  
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average for 5+ days, reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days unless sentiment strongly bullish.  
- When sentiment is mixed (±0.3–0.7), model often overfits recent noise; use 3-day rolling average of history to smooth forecast.
